step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Visual Analysis: The diagram shows an architecture for transaction processing and NLP enrichment. On the top left, an incoming arrow enters a 'Kinesis' stream. From Kinesis, an arrow points to a top 'Lambda' function. The top Lambda function interacts bi-directionally with a top 'RDS' database (a curved arrow going to RDS and a return arrow from RDS). Downwards from top Lambda, an arrow points to an 'SQS' queue. Multiple fan-out arrows lead from SQS to a bottom 'Lambda' function. From the bottom Lambda, two arrows diverge: one to a bottom 'RDS' database and another to a bottom 'Kinesis' stream.
2. Node Identification: All drawn services (Kinesis, Lambda, RDS, SQS, Lambda, RDS, Kinesis) are distinct physical boxes/icons drawn on the board. Each represents a distinct functional step in the ingestion and processing flow.
3. Exact Service Names: Validated against the schema string list ('Kinesis', 'Lambda', 'RDS', 'SQS').
4. Edge Tracing & Sequencing: Follows the visual flow starting from Kinesis (ingestion event) -> Lambda -> RDS query/response -> SQS queue -> Lambda fan-out -> RDS & Kinesis targets.

nodes.name: Ingestion Lambda

nodes.notes: Stores scraped bank transactions queried by the ingestion Lambda.

nodes.name: Transaction Queue
nodes.notes: Buffers transaction description batches to allow fanning out processing.

nodes.name: NLP Processing Lambda
nodes.notes: Runs natural language processing model to enrich transaction description strings.

nodes.name: Enriched Transaction Store
nodes.notes: Stores processed and categorized transactions along with model versions.
